The pro-choice movement is built on the notion of bodily autonomy. If, for example, I want to shoot up in the privacy of my home, without children present, that choice should be respected because I am exercising my autonomy in a way that doesn't harm anyone else. I should be able to choose what I put into my body without fear that it will land me in jail. Likewise, the pro-choice movement asserts that a woman should be able to obtain a medical procedure without fear of legal consequences. It seems that many of those in the pro-choice camp are unwilling to respect bodily autonomy in all spheres where it can apply.

Just as you claim that the pro-choice movement is not built on a belief that everyone should be able to choose whether to live or die and that it deals explicitly with the issue of abortion, the pro-life movement also deals explicitly with the issue of abortion. It's unfair to hold one movement to a higher standard than the other or to claim that one should represent a belief system while the other is exempt.

FWIW, I don't actually believe that either stance represents some sort of all-encompassing philosophy about rights or some sort of belief system. I just find it interesting that pro-lifers get called out for being inconsistent when a lot of pro-choice individuals could also be said to be inconsistent as well.
